mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a strong accommodative monetary policy stance, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM but the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of these instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp in a month but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of these instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 2% YoY but the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of these instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tightening monetary policy
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of these instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 in a month but the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of these instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong demand-side recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 10% MoM and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp, but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of these instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of other economic indicators.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains below 1% but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of these instances.
